newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israel says to pursue peace talks after Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel says to pursue peace talks after Hebron deal.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Tuesday Israel would continue peace talks with the Palestinians on all pending issues after a deal on a troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.

"If today we sign the agreement about Hebron, we can continue with all the redeployment and we can have some answers about other problems that are now on the table," Mordechai told a joint news conference with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
"I believe that we are very close to signing a Hebron agreement and immediately afterwards we will continue in all the issues on the agenda between us and the Palestinians," he added.

Mordechai held talks with Mubarak in the Red Sea resort of Hurghada as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat at the Erez crossing in Gaza in a bid to seal a deal by Christmas on a long-stymied handover of the West Bank town of Hebron.

The pullout from Hebron is seen as key to any further Israeli-PLO peace moves. Arabs view the pullout -- promised by Israel's former Labour government -- as an acid test of Netanyahu's intentions toward the Middle East peace process as a whole.
